findings.description: Wrangler .dev.vars credentials were included by COPY . . in self-host Docker images.
findings.evidence: Before the fix, an actual scratch Docker build using the repository ignore rules exported a synthetic .dev.vars file into its image. No real credential file was inspected or copied by this test.
findings.impact: Anyone able to read a locally built/published image could recover credentials from .dev.vars files present in the build context.
findings.recommendation: Exclude root and nested .dev.vars and environment variants from Docker contexts. If previous images were built with real secret files present, rotate the affected credentials and retire those images; removing files from a later image cannot revoke credentials.
verification: Before: synthetic Docker build exit0; exported .dev.vars exists=true.
Regression harness against HEAD Docker ignore rules failed with exit1; the same harness against patched rules passed with exit0.
After: python3 security/scanners/infrastructure-context-test.py passed;8 root/nested credential paths excluded;3 application/example files retained.
No claim is made that an existing published image contained credentials; rotation is conditional on historical image exposure.

findings.description: Three workflows inherited repository/organization token permissions instead of declaring the read-only permissions they require.
findings.evidence: Checkov3.3.30 reported3 CKV2_GHA_1 failures before the change; all3 files had no top-level permissions declaration. Actual repository/organization default token policy was not inspected.
findings.impact: Where repository defaults permit writes, compromised build steps could receive unnecessary GitHub token write privileges.
findings.recommendation: Set explicit permissions: contents: read, and request maintainer review of the workflow control-plane change.
verification: Before: security/reports/infrastructure-actions-before.json shows365 passed,3 failed,0 parsing errors.
After: security/reports/infrastructure-checkov-github-actions.json shows368 passed,0 failed,0 parsing errors.
Parent reviewed jobs and found no GitHub-token writes required; deployment credentials remain in existing explicit secrets.

observations: Compose publishes only127.0.0.1 and explicitly selects trusted-local local_noauth mode.
Cloudflare secret settings use Config.redacted/optionalSecret; auxiliary audit worker receives a bounded subset.
Custom-domain self-host deployments disable alternate workers.dev URL; audit worker url:false.
Access deployments fail closed with a nonempty email allow-list; live Cloudflare configuration was not queried.
Persistent database IDs were preserved; no deployment or schema mutation was performed.
limitations: Native Trivy/Checkov policies do not interpret Alchemy TypeScript or Wrangler JSONC; these observations are source review only.
